# Microsoft Graph agent identity list requests: a pinned copy of Learn's samples

This folder is an unmodified copy of four Microsoft Graph v1.0 API reference pages and the generated permission tables they include: [List agentIdentityBlueprint](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/agentidentityblueprint-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [List agentIdentity](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/agentidentity-list?view=graph-rest-1.0), [List agentIdentityBlueprint sponsors](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/agentidentityblueprint-list-sponsors?view=graph-rest-1.0) and [List agentIdentity sponsors](https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/agentidentity-list-sponsors?view=graph-rest-1.0). They come from [microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-docs-contrib](https://github.com/microsoftgraph/microsoft-graph-docs-contrib/tree/bb35043c742d4406d73ccae904c05fbfca7c7428/api-reference/v1.0) at commit `bb35043c742d4406d73ccae904c05fbfca7c7428` (October 31, 2026, UTC; retrieved October 30, 2026, US time). The pages keep their upstream folder layout for the includes (`includes/permissions/`). The repository's code license (`LICENSE-CODE`) is MIT; its documentation license (`LICENSE`) is Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International.

**Why these files.** The HTTP request samples are inline in the pages; the least-privileged permissions are in the generated tables the pages include, and the chapter's tests read both. The SDK snippets the pages include are generated from the HTTP samples and aren't copied. `examples/non-person-identity/tests/AgentIdSampleHarness.ps1` sends the samples, unmodified, to the chapter's fake Microsoft Graph. Nothing is installed and nothing signs in. The [developer workbook *Building Non-Person Identity*, Chapter 09](../../../docs/project-plans/developer-workbooks/non-person-identity/09-ai-agent-identities.md) links Learn rather than quoting the pages.

**How it stays honest.**

- `snapshot.json` records the upstream repository, paths, commit, dates, licenses, each file's git blob hash (checked against the upstream tree at that commit before the manifest was written) and the size and SHA-256 of every file here. `scripts/tests/test_third_party_snapshots.py` fails if any file is changed, added or removed.
- The weekly source watch follows commits to each upstream file (the eight `npi-graph-agentidentity*` feeds in `data/source-watch/feeds.json`) and reports each one in its issue under DW (developer workbooks).
- To move to a newer upstream commit: review the upstream change, copy the files from that commit, regenerate `snapshot.json`, rerun `examples/non-person-identity/tests/NpiAgentId.Tests.ps1` and the Chapter 09 labs, and open a pull request. Never edit the files here; changes the program needs go in `examples/non-person-identity`.

These files keep their upstream bytes, line endings included, so the hashes match the upstream commit.
